subject: Discovery recap and mutual plan — next steps & decision calendar
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@edgehealth.com>, Sasha March <sasha@edgehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T17:15:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap and suggested mutual plan (short)

Alex / Sasha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap while it's fresh and a proposed set of milestones so we can align internal stakeholders at EdgeHealth and at Redwood. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update the plan.

Key pain & goals we heard:
- Model latency spikes on nightly batch + real-time triage path impact care-coordination SLA (current 800–1200ms p50 on CPU hosts).
- Cost unpredictability when volume spikes during claims windows — you want predictable unit economics for budgeting.
- Security: SOC2 logs and tenant isolation are gating for procurement.

Success criteria for the pilot:
1) 3x reduction in tail latency for the triage path (p95 target <400ms)
2) Predictable per-token cost within 12% of committed baseline during 30-day load test
3) Proof of FedRAMP-like audit logs and encryption-in-transit at rest for trial data

Proposed mutual action plan (high level) — dates are provisional: 
- Milestone A (Pilot scope & data access): EdgeHealth provides sample throughput profile + 1 representative prompt set by 2026-10-08. (Owner: Alex)
- Milestone B (Environment & baseline run): Redwood deploys a dedicated test pool + baseline run and shares latency/cost dashboard by 2026-10-15. (Owner: Mina)
- Milestone C (Optimization & QA): Quantization / batching tuning + SLO test by 2026-10-22. (Owner: Karthik)
- Milestone D (Exec review / procurement decision): EdgeHealth procurement & security sign-off by 2026-10-29. (Owner: Sasha)

Decision process: you indicated a two-step approval (technical sign-off from data science + procurement commercial sign-off). If that changes (e.g., need legal redlines), please confirm owners and timeline.

Immediate asks: 
1) Alex — can you confirm the lead data scientist and a procurement contact by 2026-10-04?
2) Sasha — are there standard evidence packages you prefer (SOC2 + retention policy + encryption attestation)? We can attach an initial package.
3) Redwood (Ben / Karthik) — we’ll prepare a draft MPA and a one-page cost runbook for the pilot.

Attachments: draft MPA (v0.2) + SLA exceptions doc attached for procurement review.

Thanks — short and actionable. I’ll follow up on Friday with an updated MPA once I have your confirmation on owners.

—
Mina Haddad
Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
mina@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555‑0183

Mina — thanks for the crisp summary. This matches our internal notes. A few clarifications and confirmations: 

- Confirmed owners: Data Science lead is Dr. Elena Park (elena.park@edgehealth.com), Procurement lead is Sasha March (cc'd).
- Evidence package: SOC2 report + retention policy doc + a short checklist of encrypted key management is preferred — Sasha will confirm if we need KMS integration details.
- Timeline: 2026-10-08 for sample prompt set is realistic. We may need to mask/transform PII from the sample — Elena will coordinate on that.

One ask on the pilot scope: can Redwood provide an estimate of commit sizing (GPU hours / baseline throughput) so procurement has a starting point? A conservative estimate is fine; we just need a ballpark for capex/opex budgeting.

Appreciate the attachment — I’ll review the MPA draft and push it to procurement next week.

Best,
Alex

- Dedicated test pool: 2x A10G-equivalent GPUs for a 30-day trial window; expected steady throughput ~75 reqs/sec with 1.5k token average context during load tests.
- Estimated committed GPU-hours: ~1,440 GPU-hours (2 GPUs x 24 hrs x 30 days) as baseline; we can provide burst capacity on demand.
- Estimated cost guidance (hosted pilot): $X,XXX/month committed (detailed calc in the MPA spreadsheet).

We also attached the editable MPA (EdgeHealth_Mutual_Action_Plan_v0.2.xlsx) with a row-per-milestone, owners, acceptance criteria, and a slot for procurement terms. Please review the SLA exceptions doc — we included common enterprise asks and proposed mitigations.

Next practical steps (can we lock these in by COB Tue 2026-10-06):
1) EdgeHealth: confirm Elena (data science) and Sasha (procurement) as milestone owners in the attached MPA and add any legal or compliance reviewers.
2) Redwood: we’ll schedule the baseline deployment and invite a short runbook session (30 min) with Elena and your infra team on 2026-10-12.
3) Procurement: confirm whether a third-party security assessment or additional evidence is required to start procurement paperwork.

If agreeable, Mina will publish an updated MPA in Drive and share a HubSpot milestone update.
